name: Badami Chalukya Monuments
theme: The Malaprabha valley cradle of southern temple architecture — Aihole, Badami and Mahakuta, and UNESCO-listed Pattadakal
description: Along the Malaprabha river in northern Karnataka, the early Chalukyas of Badami raised the monuments where South Indian temple architecture was invented, tested, and perfected between the sixth and eighth centuries. At Aihole, the cradle, builders experimented with plan after plan, as the Durga and Lad Khan temples show. At their capital Badami they cut Shaiva, Vaishnava, and Jain caves into a red sandstone cliff and raised the Bhutanatha shrines beside Agastya Lake, with the tank-side group of Mahakuta close by and the living temple of Banashankari at Cholachagudda. At Pattadakal, inscribed by UNESCO, they brought northern and southern styles together: Sangameshwara, the oldest of the group; the great Virupaksha; and Papanatha, the northern-style experiment set apart toward the village. Seen as one circuit, the towns trace the whole birth of a tradition, an easy drive apart in the same valley.
